subject: Instrumentation & obs comparison — next tests for hyperscaler evaluation
body:
--- Message 1 of 4 ---
From: Jordan Fields <jordan@acme.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Sophie Park <sophie.park@cloudway.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo questions — obs/telemetry comparisons

Thanks again for the demo today, Marissa. The team at Acme liked the latency and throughput numbers, but we need to close the gap on operational visibility before we move to POC. A few follow-ups from our end: 

- Can you map Redwood's tracing and metrics to our SRE checklist (I've attached it). Specifically: request-level traces, KV-cache hit metrics, per-model token breakdowns, and per-tenant cost slices.
- We ran a quick test with Cloudway's managed endpoints and noticed differences in request-level sampling and trace context propagation — can Redwood reproduce those exact traces so our SREs can compare side-by-side?
- What are the observable differences we should expect when comparing Redwood Dedicated vs Cloudway-managed inference? Any known metric gaps or different aggregation windows?

Next steps from us: we can stand up a small internal test harness the week of Jul 6 if you can provide a short test plan and an instrumentation matrix we can drop into our CI.

Jordan
Senior Platform Engineer, Acme AI

--- Message 2 of 4 ---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Fields <jordan@acme.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Sophie Park <sophie.park@cloudway.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo questions — obs/telemetry comparisons

Jordan — thanks, great questions. I've put together an initial plan below and attached our instrumentation matrix (redwood-instrumentation-matrix.xlsx). High level: Redwood's observability covers all items on your checklist, but the shape and collection semantics differ in three places that will matter for a side-by-side: sampling strategy, event enrichment (tenant/model tags), and aggregation windows.

Proposed short plan for the CI harness you mentioned: 
1) Baseline run (no caching) — 1k requests across two model sizes to capture end-to-end latency and traces.
2) Cache-enabled run — measure KV-cache hit rate and token-time breakdowns.
3) Stress run to trigger autoscaling/queued requests to validate queue-time metrics and fallback behavior.
4) Trace propagation test — we will inject your trace headers and reproduce a trace that matches Cloudway's format where possible.

Deliverables we will send by Jul 6 EOD: 
- Instrumentation mapping doc (CSV) that maps Redwood metric names to your SRE checklist.
- Sample traces for the trace-propagation test and a short script to replay them.
- A short README on how to ingest our metrics into your Datadog/Grafana dashboards.

Ben, would you and/or Karthik weigh in on the trace-format gaps and whether we should add a dedicated agent to export Cloudway-compatible trace contexts?

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

--- Message 3 of 4 ---
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jordan Fields <jordan@acme.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Sophie Park <sophie.park@cloudway.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Jul 2026 11:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo questions — obs/telemetry comparisons

Marissa/Jordan — quick technical notes from the ops side: 

- Trace format: Redwood uses open-telemetry by default; trace context fields match the W3C traceparent standard. Cloudway appears to use a proprietary sampling header in front of OTLP. We can emit a compatibility header to mimic their sampling decisions for test runs; that will make side-by-side traces look similar for your SREs.
- Sampling: production sampling is adaptive (rate + error-priority). For the CI harness we recommend 100% sampling so you can inspect full traces.
- Metrics and aggregation: Redwood exposes per-request metrics with tags {tenant, model_name, model_variant, route}. Aggregation windows are 1s/10s/60s; Cloudway's managed endpoint aggregates at 60s only — expect variance in tail percentiles for short bursts.
- Per-token cost slices: we can add token-level counters emitted per-request; they do add ~2–3% CPU overhead in the tightest latencies, but acceptable for short tests.

Attachments: I included a brief PDF (hyperscaler-obs-diff.pdf) that sketches the observable deltas we expect when comparing Redwood Dedicated vs Cloudway-managed endpoints. It focuses on the operationally relevant gaps (trace context, aggregated windows, sample-rate behavior, and fallback visibility).

Proposed concrete next tests (week of Jul 6): 
A) 100% sample baseline with Cloudway-compatible header; capture 2k traces across small and medium models.
B) Cache-enabled run with token counters; capture KV-hit rates and token slices.
C) Autoscale spike to 200 RPS to expose queueing/latency tail behavior.

If that looks good, I'll stand up the env and share the run script + synthetic workload generator by Monday morning (Jul 6).

—Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com
